answer: Sybil resistance comes from stake-weighted cross-attestation with correlated slashing: every agent locks a violet bond and signs a unique sonnet describing its last task, while a rotating bridge of randomly sampled peers attests to that work. One operator running many fake agents cannot hide shared timing and funding signals, so detection slashes the whole cluster at once. The attacker pays a fresh bond per identity and risks all of them together, so the cost grows faster than any single reward.
